patients.summary: 36-year-old logistics coordinator with perinatally acquired HIV followed at an outside ID clinic and genital HSV-2 on suppression. A 2023 adherence lapse brought an unsuppressed viral load and HIV-associated thrombocytopenia that recovered with adherence; later primary syphilis (2025) and chlamydial epididymitis (2026), both treated.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer primary care here. Says his old PCP's office stopped taking his plan. Has Medicaid, verified active. Gets HIV care at an outside ID clinic and wants to keep that. Booked new patient appt 6/8 at 9:00. Records release forms emailed for prior PCP and the ID clinic; he will sign and send back.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M here to set up primary care. Transferring from a prior PCP office.

HIV since birth (mother HIV+). Followed by an outside ID clinic every ~6 mo, on Biktarvy 1 tab daily, which ID prescribes. Per pt last viral load was undetectable and CD4 'in the 600s'. No OIs that he knows of. Also genital HSV-2, on valacyclovir 500 daily for suppression for years; rare breakthrough, none recently.

PSH: circumcised as a newborn, nothing else.
Meds: Biktarvy daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Allergies: none to meds.
FH: mother HIV+. Father - doesn't know his history. Maternal grandmother with type 2 DM.
SH: works as a logistics coordinator for a distribution company. Never smoked. A drink or two on weekends. No IV or other drug use. Single, sexually active, more than one partner; says he uses condoms.
COVID: two Pfizer doses this spring at a pharmacy.

ROS: negative except as above.
Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, no thrush. No cervical/axillary nodes. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Skin without rash. GU deferred.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. HIV, perinatal, stable per report - continue care with ID. Records requested. Will keep copies of their labs here.
2. Genital HSV-2 - continue valacyclovir; I can handle refills.
3. Health maintenance - PCV20 and first MenACWY today (both recommended with HIV). Second MenACWY in 8 wk, nurse visit. Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids, UA.
Follow up yearly for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Malik - your kidney and liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol and urine all came back normal. Nice to have a baseline on file here. We'll see you in August for the second meningitis shot.

documents.title: Records From Prior PCP and ID Clinic
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 38 pages by fax, prior primary care office plus the outside ID clinic.

Prior PCP: routine visits, problem list HIV (perinatal) and genital HSV-2. Allergies NKDA. COVID mRNA doses x2 spring 2021 entered from the pharmacy record. No other screening due at his age.

ID clinic: most recent visit April 2021. HIV-1 RNA not detected, CD4 in the normal range, on bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily with good adherence documented. Plan: q6 month follow-up with labs.

Abstracted into chart. Forwarded to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for 2nd MenACWY. No problems after the first one. Given 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, left after 15 min. Series complete; booster due in 5 years.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: After-work slot. Flu vaccine R deltoid, Pfizer booster L deltoid. Feels well, no fever. Observed 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC - Visit 11/16/2021
Re: Malik Hughes

Six-month visit for perinatally acquired HIV. Doing well, no missed doses he can think of. No fevers, weight steady. HSV quiet on valacyclovir.
Allergies: NKDA.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF 1 tab daily; valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Exam unremarkable, no oral lesions, no adenopathy.
Labs: HIV-1 RNA not detected. CD4 stable.
Plan: continue current regimen, return in 6 months. Thank you for sharing his care.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, can I get a refill on the valacyclovir? Down to like 5 pills. Same pharmacy. Thanks

documents.title: RE: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent to your pharmacy, 90 days with 3 refills.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. No concerns. Last ID visit in Nov was fine, next one is June. Taking Biktarvy and valacyclovir daily, no HSV outbreaks this year.
SH unchanged. Long shifts at the warehouse office lately, sleeping ok. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk.
PHQ-2: 0.
Exam: NAD. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Skin clear. Ext normal.

A/P: healthy 32M with well-controlled HIV per ID.
- CMP, CBC, lipids today.
- Vaccines: flu/COVID this fall.
- Safer sex reviewed, he gets STI screens through ID.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Annual Labs Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, CBC, lipids normal. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside ID clinic, seen 6/14/22.

HIV, acquired perinatally, on BIC/FTC/TAF. Reports taking it every day. No new symptoms. No new partners since his last visit per his report.
NKDA. Meds unchanged.
Exam: well, no lymphadenopathy, no oral candidiasis, skin clear.
Viral load remains undetectable; CD4 holding steady. RPR non-reactive.
Continue regimen. Next visit December.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L arm) and Pfizer bivalent booster (R arm). Afebrile, feels fine. No reaction during observation. Pt reminded about his ID appt in December.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE - outside clinic letter
Date of visit: 12/06/2022

Routine HIV visit. He feels well. Says work has been hectic with holiday shipping. Adherence reported as good, though he admits a couple of late doses.
Allergies: none known.
Medications: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily, valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Exam: normal.
Results: HIV RNA undetectable. CD4 stable.
Assessment/plan: virologically suppressed. Continue. Return in about 3 months for routine check.
